## Checklist

Delete any section that genuinely does not apply, rather than leaving it unticked and ambiguous.

Implementation:
- [ ] The acceptance criteria are demonstrably met, not just asserted
- [ ] Nothing is hard-coded that belongs in settings
- [ ] There is no leftover TODO without a linked ticket

Tests:
- [ ] Unit tests cover the logic and its branches
- [ ] Integration tests cover anything touching the database
- [ ] The failure paths are tested, not only the happy path
- [ ] make check passes locally

Security:
- [ ] The change declares its required permission, or is explicitly public
- [ ] Input is validated at the boundary
- [ ] Ownership is filtered inside the query, not checked afterward
- [ ] No secret is committed

Data, if there is a migration:
- [ ] The migration was read line by line, not just autogenerated and trusted
- [ ] It is tested in both the upgrade and the downgrade direction
- [ ] It is backward-compatible with the currently running version
- [ ] New query paths have their indexes considered, justified with query plans

Observability:
- [ ] The change emits logs for its business events
- [ ] Anything that can fail in production has an alert and a runbook

Human validation:
- [ ] I ran this and verified it myself, and I have said on which machine below
- [ ] It has a review from the other track

Verified on: macOS / Windows / both

## Honesty check

Note anything that is implemented but not yet verified, anything you could not test, and anything left deliberately for a follow-up. This section being empty is usually a sign nobody looked closely, so prefer honesty over a clean-looking template.
